_source: Athena_Explains (27.8K subs) Short, a pilot who saved 167 passengers, 7.4M views, 49 s, auto-dubbed. Built-in browser 2026-11-20: played 0-47 s with the audio probe, frames every ~6 s; the last ~2 s not captured (autoplay moved on). SAMPLED. Our own descriptions.

hook.firstFrame: a grey 3D cockpit with two pilots (one a stiff faceless figure), a round real photo of the captain inset at the top
hook.firstLine: (auto-dubbed; names the pilot and the 167 passengers he saved)

shots.picture: 3D cockpit, pilots at the controls, circular real portrait of the captain at the top
fast cuts (about one a second) between cabin, cockpit and map angles
tilted 3D map: white land extruded from black, origin and destination red with yellow tag labels
a small white jet in a black void over a white grid floor, yellow boxed altitude label
white faceless mannequins in a grey cabin, blue seats the only colour
fuselage cutaway on the grid floor: rows of seats, passengers coloured red or green
(sampled sparsely) more cabin and cockpit angles

whyItWorks: A real face (round photo inset) over a 3D set in frame one: the hero is a person, not a plane.
Ten cuts in the first ten seconds, then 5-7 s 3D shots: fast hook, slower explanation.
Untextured clay 3D (white mannequins, one accent colour) reads instantly at phone size.
Colour coding on a cutaway (red vs green passengers) carries the stakes without words.
